translations.text: There is one beginning of all things, that is, God Almighty. He is the beginning and the end: he is the beginning because he always was;
He is the end without any ending, because he is ever unending. He is King of all kings and Lord of all lords.
With his might he holds the heavens and the earth and all creatures without toil, and he looks upon the abysses that are beneath this earth.
He moves all the mountains with one hand, and nothing can withstand his will. No creature can perfectly contemplate or understand God.
Angels have greater knowledge of God than men, and yet they cannot perfectly understand God.
He created creatures when he wished; through his wisdom he made all things, and through his will he gave them all life.

This Trinity is one God; that is, the Father, and his Wisdom, ever begotten of himself; and the Will of them both, that is, the Holy Spirit: he is not begotten, but he proceeds from the Father and from the Son alike.
These three persons are one Almighty God, who made the heavens and the earth and all creatures.
He created ten hosts of angels, that is, angels and archangels, thrones, dominions, principalities, powers, virtues, cherubim, seraphim.
Here are nine hosts of angels. They have no body, but they are all spirits, very strong and mighty and beautiful, created in great fairness, to the praise and honour of their Creator.
The tenth host fell away and turned to evil. God created them all good and let them have their own choice, whether they would love and follow their Creator or forsake him.
Now the leader of the tenth host was created very fair and beautiful, so that he was called Light-bearer.

Then he began to grow proud because of the beauty that he had, and said in his heart that he wished to be, and easily could be, like his Creator, and to sit in the northern part of the kingdom of heaven, and to have power and dominion against God Almighty.
Then he settled this plan with the host that he ruled over, and they all inclined to that plan.
When they had all settled this plan among themselves, God's wrath came upon them all, and they were all changed from the fair form in which they had been created into loathsome devils.
And very justly it befell him so, when he wished through pride to be better than he was created, and said that he could be like Almighty God.
Then he and all his companions became more wicked and worse than any other creature; and while he was considering how he might share dominion with God,

in the meantime the Almighty Creator prepared the torment of hell for him and his companions, and drove them all out of the joy of the kingdom of heaven, and let them fall into the eternal fire that was prepared for them because of their arrogance.
Then at once the nine hosts that were left there bowed to their Creator with all humility, and committed their counsel to his will.
Then Almighty God confirmed the nine hosts of angels, and established them so firmly that they never afterwards could or would turn away from his will;
nor can they now, nor will they, commit any sin, but they are ever intent on this one thing: how they may obey God and please him.
The others who fell there could also have done so, if they had wished; because God made them of the beautiful nature of angels, and let them have their own choice,
and he never inclined or compelled them by any means to that evil plan; nor did the evil plan ever come from God's thought, but it came from the devil's, as we said before.
Now many a man thinks and wonders where the devil came from; let him know, then, that God created as a glorious angel the one who is now the devil; but God did not create him as a devil;
but when he was utterly ruined and made guilty through his great arrogance and hostility, then he who had before been made a glorious angel was turned into a devil.
Then God wished to fill up and make good the loss that had been lost from the heavenly host, and said that he would make man from earth,
that earthly man should prosper and earn through humility the dwellings in the kingdom of heaven which the devil forfeited through pride.
Then God made a man out of clay, breathed a spirit into him and gave him life, and so he became a man created in soul and in body.
God gave him the name Adam, and for a while he was standing alone. Then God brought him into Paradise, settled him there, and said to him,
"You may enjoy all the things that are in Paradise, and they are all entrusted to you, except one tree that stands in the middle of Paradise.
Do not touch the fruit of that tree, because you will become mortal if you eat the fruit of that tree."
Why would God deny him so small a thing, when he had entrusted so many other great things to him?
Yes, but how could Adam recognise what he was, unless he was obedient to his Lord in some matter? It is as if God had said to him,
"You will not know that I am your Lord and that you are my servant unless you do what I command you and keep away from what I forbid you.

What then can it be that you must refrain from? I tell you, refrain from the fruit of one tree, and by that easy obedience you will earn the joy of the kingdom of heaven and the place from which the devil fell through disobedience."
If, then, you break this little command, you shall die the death."
And Adam was so wise that God brought to him the cattle, and the kinds of wild animals, and the kinds of birds, when he had created them;
And Adam gave names to all of them, and they are still called by the names he gave them then. Then God said,
"It is not fitting that this man should be alone and have no helper. Let us make him a mate, to be a help and a comfort to him."
And God then put Adam to sleep, and while he slept he took a rib from his side, and made a woman from that rib, and asked Adam what she should be called.
Then Adam said, "She is bone of my bones and flesh of my flesh; let her name be Virago, that is, woman, because she is taken from her man."
Then Adam afterwards gave her another name, Eve, that is, life, because she is the mother of all the living.
All creatures—the heavens and angels, sun and moon, stars and earth, all cattle and birds, the sea and all fish, and all creatures—God created and made in six days;
and on the seventh day he finished his work, and then rested and hallowed the seventh day, because on that day he finished his work.
And he looked at all the works he had made, and they were all very good. He made all things without any pre-existing material. He said,
"Let there be light," and at once light came into being. Again he said, "Let there be heaven," and at once heaven was made, just as he had planned it with his wisdom and his will.
He spoke again and commanded the earth to bring forth living beasts; and he then created from the earth every kind of beast and every kind of wild animal, all those that go on four feet;
likewise from water he created fish and birds, and gave the fish swimming and the birds flight; but he gave no soul to any beast or any fish;
but their blood is their life, and as soon as they are dead, they are entirely ended.
When he made the man Adam, he did not say, "Let a man be made," but he said,
"Let us make man in our likeness." Then he made the man with his hands and breathed a soul into him. Therefore man, if he thrives in goodness, is better than all the animals,
because they will all come to nothing, but man is eternal in one part, that is, in the soul, which will never end.
The body is mortal through Adam's guilt, but nevertheless God will raise up the body again to eternal things on Judgement Day.
Now heretics have said that the devil created some creatures, but they lie; he cannot create any creatures, because he is not a Creator,
but [he] is a hideous fiend, and with lies he seeks to deceive and destroy the unwary; but he cannot compel any man to any sin unless the man of his own will submits to his teaching.
Whatever in creation seems hostile and harms men, that is all because of our sins and evil deserts.

Then the devil perceived that Adam and Eve were created for this purpose: that they should by humility and obedience earn the dwelling in the kingdom of heaven from which he had fallen because of his pride,
Then he felt great anger and envy towards the humans, and considered how he could destroy them. He came to the two humans in the form of a serpent, first to the woman, and said to her,
"Why did God forbid you the fruit of the tree that stands in the middle of Paradise?" Then the woman said,
"God forbade us the fruit of that tree, and said that we would die if we tasted it." Then the devil said,
"It is not as you say. God knows very well that if you eat from that tree, your eyes will be opened, and you will be able to see and recognise both good and evil, and you will be like angels."
They were not created blind, but God created them so innocent that they knew nothing evil, neither in sight, nor in speech, nor in deed.
Yet the woman was then led astray through the devil's teaching, and took of the tree's fruit, and ate, and gave it to her husband, and he ate.
Then they were both mortal, and knew both good and evil; and they were then naked, and were ashamed of it.
Then God came and asked why he had broken his command. He drove them both out of Paradise and said,

"Because you obeyed your wife's words and scorned my command, you will have to toil for your food with hardship, and the earth, which is cursed because of your deed, will give you thorns and brambles.
You were taken from earth, and you shall return to earth. You are dust, and you shall return to dust." Then God made them garments of skins, and they were clothed with those skins.
The dead skins signified that they were now mortal who could have been immortal, if they had kept that easy commandment of God.
Neither Adam nor all mankind that afterwards descended from him would ever have needed to taste death, if that tree had been allowed to stand untouched, and no one had tasted of it;
but Adam and his offspring would have bred at appointed times, just as clean animals do now, and afterwards all would have gone without death to the eternal life.
It was not ordained for him by God, nor was he compelled to break God's command; but God left him free and gave him his own choice, whether he would be obedient or disobedient.
He then became obedient to the devil and disobedient to God, and he and all mankind were handed over, after this life, into the torment of hell, with the devil who had led him astray.
Yet God knew that he had been led astray, and considered how he might again have mercy on him and on all mankind.
God had endowed the soul of man with two things: that is, with immortality and with happiness.
Then through the devil's treachery and Adam's guilt we lost the happiness of our soul, but we did not lose the immortality;
it is eternal and never ends, though the body ends, which shall afterwards rise again through God's might to an eternal dwelling.
Adam then lived on in this life with toil, and he and his wife then begot children, both sons and daughters;
and he lived nine hundred and thirty years, and then died, just as had been promised him before, because of that guilt; and his soul went to hell.
Now some people ask where his soul came from: whether from the father or from the mother?
We say from neither of them; but the same God who created Adam with his hands creates every person's body in the mother's womb;
and the same one who breathed into Adam's body and gave him a soul, that same one gives children soul and life in their mother's womb when they are formed;
and he lets them have their own free choice when they are grown, just as Adam had.
Then mankind quickly grew numerous, and very many turned to evil, and angered God with various sins, and most of all with fornication.
Then God was so greatly angered by the wicked deeds of men that he said he regretted that he had ever created mankind.
Yet there was one man righteous before God, who was called Noah. Then God said to him,

"I will destroy all mankind with water because of their sins, but I will save you alone, and your wife, and your three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their three wives, because you are righteous and pleasing to me.
Now make yourself an ark, three hundred fathoms long, fifty fathoms wide and thirty fathoms high: roof it all over, and smear all the seams with tar, and afterwards go in with your household.
I will gather in to you, of every kind of beast and of every kind of bird, always a pair of mates, so that they may afterwards be for breeding. I will send a flood over all the world."

He then did as God commanded him, and God shut them inside the ark and sent rain from heaven for forty days together, and at the same time opened all the springs and water-channels of the great abyss.
The flood then grew and bore up the ark, and it rose over all the hills.
Then every living thing was drowned except those who were inside the ark; from them the whole world was afterwards re-established.
Then God promised that he would never again kill all mankind with water, and said to Noah and to his sons, "I will set my covenant between me and you as a sign of this promise;
that is, when I cover the heavens with clouds, then my rainbow will appear among the clouds, and then I will remember my covenant, that from now on I will not drown mankind with water."
Noah lived nine hundred and fifty years in all his life, before the flood and after the flood, and then he died.
Then for some time after the flood the fear of God was among mankind, and they all had one language.
Then they said among themselves that they would build a city, and a tower within the city so high that its roof would rise up to the heavens; and then they began to build.
Then God came there while they were working hardest, and gave each man who was there a separate language.
Then there were as many languages there as there were men, and none of them knew what another said. And they then stopped the building and scattered throughout the whole world.

Then afterwards mankind was deceived by the devil and turned away from faith in God, so that they made themselves images, some of gold, some of silver, some also of stone, some of wood, and gave them names;
the names of those men who were giants and evildoers. Then, once they were dead, the living said that they were gods, and worshipped them, and offered sacrifices to them;
and then the devils came to their images, lived in them, and spoke to men as if they were gods;
and the deceived people fell on their knees before the images and said, "You are our gods, and we place our faith and our hope in you."
Then this error sprang up throughout the whole world, and the true Creator, who alone is God, was scorned and dishonoured.
Yet there was one family that never bowed to any idol, but always worshipped the true God. That family sprang from Noah's eldest son, who was called Shem:
he lived six hundred years, and his son was called Arphaxad, who lived three hundred and thirty-three years, and his son was called Shelah, who lived four hundred and thirty-three years;

then he fathered a son who was called Eber, from whom sprang the Hebrew people, whom God loved; and from that people came all the patriarchs and prophets who made known Christ's coming into this life;
that he, who was always God with the exalted Father, would become man close to the end of this world, for our redemption.
And God gave and established the law for this people, and he led them over the sea with dry feet, and he fed them for forty years with heavenly bread, and worked many wonders among that people;
because he wished to choose a mother for himself from this family.
Then at last, when the time came that God had foreseen, he sent his angel Gabriel to a maiden of that lineage, who was called Mary.
Then the angel came to her and greeted her with God's words, and made known to her that the Son of God would be born of her without union with a man.
And she then believed his words and became with child. When her time came she gave birth, and remained a virgin. That child is born twice:
he is born of the Father in heaven, without any mother, and again, when he became man, he was born of the pure virgin Mary, without any earthly father.
God the Father made mankind and all creatures through the Son, and afterwards, when we were ruined by sin, he sent the same Son for our redemption.
Then the holy mother Mary brought up the child with great reverence, and he grew as other children do, except for sin alone.
He was born without sins, and his whole life was without sins. Yet he worked no miracles openly before he was thirty years old in his human nature:
then afterwards he chose disciples for himself; first twelve, whom we call apostles, which means messengers.
Then he chose seventy-two, who are called disciples, that is, followers. Then he worked many miracles, so that people might believe that he was the Son of God.

He turned water into wine, and walked over the sea with dry feet, and he calmed the winds by his command, and he gave sight to blind men, and the power to walk properly to the halt and the lame, and smooth skin to lepers, and health to their bodies;
to the dumb he gave speech, and to the deaf hearing; to those possessed by devils and to the mad he gave their wits, and drove out the devils, and he healed every sickness;
he raised dead men from their graves to life; and he taught the people he came to with great wisdom;
and he said that no one can be saved unless he believes rightly in God, and is baptized, and adorns his faith with good works;
he shunned every wrong and all falsehood, and taught righteousness and truth.
Then the Jewish people took great offence at his teaching, and considered how they might put him to death.
Then one of the twelve companions of Christ, who was called Judas, was led astray by the devil's prompting, and he went to the Jewish people and plotted with them how he might betray Christ to them.
Even if all humankind were gathered together, they could not all kill him if he himself did not wish it;
for he came to us because he wished to suffer death for us, and so by his own death to redeem from the torment of hell all mankind who believe.

He would not take us by force out of the devil's power unless the devil forfeited it; and the devil forfeited it thoroughly when he incited and urged the hearts of the Jewish men to the killing of Christ.
Christ then allowed the cruel men to seize him and bind him, and to kill him by hanging on a cross.
Lo, then two believing men buried him honourably, and Christ in the meantime went to hell, and overpowered the devil, and took from him Adam and Eve and their offspring,
[?] the part that had pleased him before, and led them to their bodies, and rose from death with that great host on the third day after his passion.
Then he came to his apostles and comforted them, and stayed with them for a period of forty days;
and he repeated the same teaching that he had taught them before, and commanded them to go throughout the whole world, preaching baptism and the true faith.

Then on the fortieth day after his resurrection the Lord ascended to heaven, before the eyes of them all, in the same body in which he had suffered, and he sits at the right hand of his Father and rules all creation.
He has opened the way into his kingdom for righteous people, and those who utterly despise his commandments will be sunk in hell.
Truly, he will come at the end of this world with great majesty in the clouds, and all those who have ever received a soul will rise from death to meet him;

and then he will hand over the wicked to the devil, into the eternal fire of the torment of hell; the righteous he will bring with him into the kingdom of heaven, in which they will reign forever in eternity.
Dearest people, consider this saying, and with great care turn away from unrighteousness, and earn with good works eternal life with God, who alone reigns in eternity. Amen.
